text:
Sam Reinhart reached 700 career points in St. Louis, and his 12 goals in 22 games look sturdy. He has 12.96 expected goals (the quality of his chances), so he is finishing right about where he should, and his chance quality per 60 minutes is up from 1.28 last season to 1.76. He's on a four-game point streak with 7 goals in his last ten games.

The worry sits at five-on-five. Florida gets only 46% of the expected goals with him on the ice, about 7.7 points worse than when he sits, yet the team has scored 9.7 more goals than those chances deserve. That on-ice luck is padding his 22 points, and it tends to fade.

Context helps him. Evolving-Hockey had his competition in the 97th percentile last season, and most of his value came on the penalty kill. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him getting 1.8 shots per 60 off passes across the slot or from behind the net, the most dangerous kind. Watch whether Florida's five-on-five share with him climbs; his own shooting looks fine.
headline: Reinhart hits 700 with goals that hold up
